newsitem.title: UK: NWE HS fuel barges firm on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE HS fuel barges firm on tight supply.

text.p: Euro high sulphur fuel barges firmed on Monday on a shortage of prompt material caused by loading problems, traders said.
With the low sulphur market in contango a cargo loading later in August achieved better numbers than a vessel done for nearer prompt delivery.
Traders said high sulphur barges changed hands at $95 fob ARA three times after earlier trades at $94 and $94.25 a tonne, compared with Friday's trading range of $92.50 to $93.50.
"There's a shortage of prompt avails as some people had problems over the weekend," one trader said, explaining the move to the upside.
"A major was buying and not selling today. Seems they are having a problem and another seller is out of fuel and the majors are not offering," a second trader said.
But other traders said with Russian material expected to arrive soon the market will come off a little.
High sulphur cargoes were valued stronger at the $89 mark with supplies said to be scarce. A deal at the weekend for Russian cracked was reported to have been done at two means plus $2.50.
However, one seller dismissed reports of a shortage of supply saying he will have seven Russian cracked cargoes coming in soon. Others said that some of them are already committed.

One percent cargoes were firmer, with an end month 40,000-tonne cargo said sold by a major at $95.25 fob after a deal earlier in the day at $92.50 for a smaller August 20-25 loader sold by a French-based major.
Traders said the second cargo fetched better numbers due to its bigger size, better shipping economics and with the market in contango.
Low sulphur fuel barges were offered $1 lower at $96 by some sellers but no buyers were found.
